{{quote:

> — [The Will and Testament of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá](https://anis.oceanlibrary.com/doc/the-will-and-testament-of-abdul-baha-20920#p17)

'Abdu'l-Bahá describes science as the *"discoverer of realities"* and says it is of two kinds:

{{quote:

> "Scientific knowledge is the highest attainment upon the human plane, for science is the discoverer of realities. It is of two kinds: material and spiritual. Material science is the investigation of natural phenomena; divine science is the discovery and realization of spiritual verities."  
> — [Social Action](https://oceanlibrary.com/social-action_bahaullah/?paraId=para_250&selectionString=social_action_ocean_en-bl7h.0~social_action_ocean_en-bl7h.462)

P1}}
{{quote:

> "from the beginning of man's existence he is a distinct species. ...his species (naw') and essence (máhíyah) undergo no change. ...Man was always a distinct species, a man, not an animal."  
> — [Divine Philosophy](https://oceanlibrary.com/divine-philosophy_abdul-baha)

P17}}
Bahá'u'lláh makes knowledge a duty:

{{quote:

> "Arts, crafts and sciences uplift the world of being, and are conducive to its exaltation. Knowledge is as wings to man's life, and a ladder for his ascent. Its acquisition is incumbent upon everyone."  
> — [Bahá’í Sacred Writings](https://oceanlibrary.com/bahai-sacred-writings/?paraId=para_677&selectionString=baha_i_sacred_writings_en-blld.0~baha_i_sacred_writings_en-blld.423)

P3}}
{{quote:

> "Although to acquire the sciences and arts is the greatest glory of mankind, this is so only on condition that man's river flow into the mighty sea, and draw from God's ancient source His inspiration."  
> — [Selections from the Writings of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá](https://oceanlibrary.com/selections-from-the-writings-of-abdul-baha/?paraId=para_517&selectionString=selections_from_the_writings_of_the_abdu_l_baha_en_j3.0~selections_from_the_writings_of_the_abdu_l_baha_en_j3.498)

P2}}

live_text_events:
The Writings start from the point that God's own reality cannot be divided or enter into anything:

{{quote:

> "The reality of the Divinity is sanctified and exalted beyond the comprehension of all created things, can in no wise be imagined by mortal mind and understanding, and transcends all human conception. That reality admits of no division, for division and multiplicity are among the characteristics of created and hence contingent things, and not accidents impinging upon the Necessary Being."  
> — [Some Answered Questions](https://anis.oceanlibrary.com/doc/some-answered-questions-abdul-baha-20911#p300)

P1}}
'Abdu'l-Bahá gives them two stations:

{{quote:

> "The Holy Manifestations of God possess two stations: one is the physical station, and one the spiritual. In other words, one station is that of a human being, and one, of the Divine Reality."  
> — [Selections from the Writings of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá](https://oceanlibrary.com/selections-from-the-writings-of-abdul-baha/?paraId=para_231&selectionString=selections_from_the_writings_of_the_abdu_l_baha_en_9v.0~selections_from_the_writings_of_the_abdu_l_baha_en_9v.261)

P2}}
Christ was a perfectly polished mirror in which the Sun of Truth appeared in the fullness of its attributes, without the Sun descending into the mirror:

{{quote:

> "The Sun of Truth, the Essence of the Divinity, appeared in that mirror and manifested its light and heat therein, yet it did not descend from the heights of holiness and the heaven of sanctity to reside within it."  
> — [Some Answered Questions](https://oceanlibrary.com/some-answered-questions_abdul-baha/?paraId=para_394&selectionString=some-answered-questions-prod-version_en_dy.0~some-answered-questions-prod-version_en_dy.765)

P3}}
